method.description: Authoring only. Five candidate authority-asset rows for the next successor tranche, every value taken from the document's own integrated source contract. The adopted Edition 1.2 archive was read to establish what each row supersedes: its four Massachusetts source-gated entries were extracted and hashed, and its STATE_MANIFEST.csv rows were read for the workflow key, revision, structural class and field count each currently carries.

scopeOfThisJob.authors: five candidate authority-asset rows and the supersession each one implies
doesNotAuthor: a sixth row for the OCP petition's Part A box 4, which is a selection inside one form
any receipt — a receipt is rcap-ma-source-materialization's artifact and that job is deliberately blocked behind this one
any amendment to Edition 1.3, which is published and immutable
any correction to the source-artifact registry or the acquisition queue, both of which are forbidden paths here
scopeOfThisJob.admissionIsNotThisJobs: These are candidates. The successor plan admits or defers each against its own eight criteria, and the deferrals this record predicts are recorded below rather than argued away.

edition13Impact.requiresNewBytesNote: True at the record level because two of the five rows carry bytes no adopted edition holds. It is not true of all five, and the per-row requiresNewBytes flag is the accurate one: three rows are metadata corrections over bytes Edition 1.2 already holds at an identical digest.
edition13Impact.requiresLicenseDispositionNote: The Commonwealth publishes these forms free, without login and without fee, and no redistribution or commercial-use restriction is published on the forms index or the how-to pages. A Commonwealth copyright and service-mark notice is present. That is an absence of a published restriction, not an affirmative grant, and it is recorded as unresolved rather than as permission. Availability is not permission.
edition13Impact.editionThirteenUntouched: Edition 1.3 is published and immutable. It was not amended, not reopened and not republished. These rows are for the tranche after it.

consumerLimitationThisRecordCannotFix.statement: The successor planner reads one asset row per decision record. assetRowFrom() in scripts/lib/rcap-factory/edition-successor.mjs reads decision.edition13AssetSpecification.assetRow, singular. This assignment requires five rows in one record, so the planner will read none of them and every row will defer as 'the decision requires new bytes and supplies no measured asset row'.
consumerLimitationThisRecordCannotFix.whyNotWorkedAround: Setting assetRow to one of the five would admit or defer that one on its merits and silently drop the other four, which is worse than a legible deferral: MA would appear to have contributed a single document. The plural key is the honest shape and the deferral it produces names the gap.
consumerLimitationThisRecordCannotFix.practicalEffectToday: None of the five could be admitted at this commit in any case. Admission requires the bytes to be locatable beneath the materialization root by digest, and no Massachusetts binary is materialized — that is rcap-ma-source-materialization's work and it is blocked behind this record by design.
consumerLimitationThisRecordCannotFix.whenItBites: After materialization lands. At that point these rows should become admissible on their merits and would still read as an absent measurement.
consumerLimitationThisRecordCannotFix.correctionRequired: Teach assetRowFrom to read an assetRows array alongside the singular assetRow, mapping each element through the same field-name alternatives it already tolerates, and emit one candidate per row.
consumerLimitationThisRecordCannotFix.correctionOwner: the factory/platform owner. scripts/lib/rcap-factory/edition-successor.mjs is a shared library and is outside this job's owned paths; it is stated here and deliberately not applied.

structuralSummary.denominatorNote: Every one of the five has terminal field count equal to widget annotation count, so no row carries a competing field denominator. The MPS shell's zero is a real zero: a dynamic XFA form with no AcroForm widget shadow has no fillable widget layer at all.

downstreamConsequences.rendererLane: Four of the five carry xfa true. rendererLane() in scripts/lib/rcap-official-pdf-production-queue.mjs tests xfa before any structural-class branch, so all four resolve to nonrenderable_source_policy_required regardless of how many widgets they carry. Only the OCP petition is an AcroForm-fill candidate on structure, and it is still source-gated on licence.
downstreamConsequences.policyOwner: PLAT-03-non-renderable-source-policy — 'Decide the approved handling for docx, html, encrypted and scanned sources'. Four Massachusetts documents now sit in its scope.
downstreamConsequences.dispositionEffectOfAssetClass: These rows propose assetClass source_gated, which is what Edition 1.2 already carries for the four it holds. If a later owner promotes any of them to packet_form, officialPdfDisposition() flips that identity from source_gated_identity to legal_design_or_technical_policy_blocked, because the branch requires exact_source_requirement_ready plus nonrenderable_source_policy_required plus a packet_form authority asset. That is a policy gate, not a regression, and it should be entered deliberately rather than discovered.
downstreamConsequences.materializationOwner: rcap-ma-source-materialization installs the bytes, reverifies them and writes one receipt per document. It is blocked behind this record by design: a receipt written before the controlling successor identity is admitted pins bytes to an identity the authority layer has not issued.
downstreamConsequences.predictedSuccessorPlanOutcomeAtThisCommi: All five defer. The three metadata corrections defer only because of the singular-assetRow reader; the two new-bytes rows would additionally defer on exact_bytes_where_applicable until materialization lands, and all five would defer on license_resolved while the commercial-use question is an absence rather than a grant. No row is silently omitted.
